biological_growth.name: Biological Growth: Life Finds a Way
biological_growth.truth: Growth doesn't follow blueprints. It follows rules that respond to environment — and what emerges surprises even the rules.
biological_growth.qfep_connection: Biological growth IS the φ term — the rate of entropy change over time. Slime mold finds shortest paths. Mushrooms colonize. Cracks propagate along stress. Each system increases or decreases local entropy through growth. The queer signature: growth that doesn't optimize, just persists.
biological_growth.description: Algorithms inspired by biological growth processes. Slime mold solves mazes, mushroom mycelium networks, crack propagation follows stress fields, and tree generation builds branching forms. Nature's algorithms — no central planner, no global view, just local rules and time.
learning_objectives: Physarum transport networks — slime mold as optimization
Crack propagation — stress creates paths of least resistance
content: BG_Slime_Mold: Physarum polycephalum simulation — the organism that solves mazes and redesigns Tokyo's rail network
BG_Mushroom_Growth: Mycelium network expansion — colonization, resource transport, fairy rings
BG_Crack_Propagation: Stress-driven fracture patterns — cracks as cellular automata following material grain
BG_Tree_Forms: Procedural tree generation — parametric branching, wind response, seasonal variation
